profile.headline: Software Engineer at Deloitte Digital
profile.summary:
Mike Kim is a Software Engineer III with over six years of full stack engineering experience across mobile, web, and enterprise applications. He joined Deloitte in January 2024 and specializes in React, React Native, Next.js, and modern JavaScript ecosystems, with backend experience building Python services using FastAPI and Flask. His recent work with generative AI tools — including Claude, OpenAI, Cursor, and Google Gemini — positions him as a practitioner at the intersection of traditional software engineering and AI-accelerated delivery. 

At Deloitte, Mike has delivered across engagements spanning logistics, life sciences, nonprofit, and internal platform development. He is known for end-to-end feature ownership, API integration work, mentoring junior engineers, and proactively improving code quality and team practices. Most recently, he has been contributing as a forward-deployed engineer and participating in FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer) training programs to deepen his client-facing delivery skills.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Full stack engineer delivering React/Next.js web and mobile apps across client-facing and internal engagements spanning logistics, life sciences, enterprise software, and platform development.

Key engagements:

• R360: Software Engineer on a React Native/Salesforce mobile app surfacing client data from Jupiter, IQ, and Factiva for ~6,281 PPMD users. Owned API integrations, built reusable components, implemented React Query. Built in 3 months, selected over Salesforce's own solution, featured at Dreamforce.

• Consumer Prototype (Logistics): Senior Software Engineer delivering a responsive MVP in 6 weeks — Consumer Hub, tracking, AI search/recommendations, and dashboards. Q4 Applause Award.

• Ascend (FDE): Forward-deployed engineer building AI tools using Claude, Python/FastAPI/Flask, and React/Next.js to ingest transcripts, emails, and surveys and surface insights.

• DP&I Resource Library & CoP Opt-In: Built Meilisearch indexing, Featured Collections, Resource Voting, and admin scripts updating 10,000+ records.

• NETO-MX: Instructor onboarding ~20 new engineers in React in Querétaro, Mexico. Created 5 modules, organized 3 panels. Q2 Applause Award.

• Smartbench: Led Bio Generator team of 3 (OpenAI); solo-built Pricing Model POC (Cursor).

• 2026 Winter Olympics: Integrated Google Gemini API into an Orb Generator for a client-facing Milan-Cortina activation.

• PharmAssist: Built frontend chatbot UI and contributed to a RAG spike using LLMs for a pharma client.

• BWDC: Implemented AWS Cognito PKCE auth flow and mapping spike for urgent team need.

• DevOps Smartbench: Deployed Coolify and Hoppscotch on AWS/Kubernetes with Pulumi.

Tech: React, React Native, Next.js, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, Flask, Tailwind, Salesforce, Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Meilisearch, AWS, Kubernetes, Cursor, Jest

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
Full stack software engineer contributing to a diverse client portfolio spanning clinical research, nonprofit, financial services, and insurance. Worked across the full product lifecycle from early-stage POCs to nationally recognized production applications.

Key engagements:

• WCG Clinical: Helped develop an internal data service API to improve the quality and efficiency of clinical trials. Built a Python FastAPI layer that ingested native Hasura actions and processed/forwarded requests to the database. Tech: Python FastAPI, Hasura, GraphQL, Docker, Postman, Docusaurus, AWS, PostgreSQL.

• Ocean Conservancy: Oversaw implementation of Trash Trap, a new feature on the Clean Swell ocean cleanup app, coinciding with the national cleanup event. Maintained and improved existing cleanup pathway features where users enter data used by the University of Toronto. Tech: React Native, Android Studio, Xcode, MySQL, Styled Components, Redux.

• Black Wealth Data Center: Helped refactor and implement extensive features for the BWDC website including wealth indicator tools and Tableau chart integrations. Involved in development from POC through national recognition. Tech: Next.js, SASS, Contentful CMS, Redis, GCP, AWS, React Context, Tableau.

• Guardian Life: Helped develop a group insurance offering from POC to production for actual customers — a mobile-friendly web app with dental and vision insurance products. Tech: Next.js, NestJS, Redis, PostgreSQL, AWS, Styled Components, Redux, RTK Query.

• City Meals on Wheels: Short-term project building a Python app to optimize meal delivery routes for drivers.

• Giant Machines Website: Involved in refactoring and improving the company website on WordPress.

• Interviews: Served as interviewer, helping interview candidates and review resumes for engineering roles.

projects.title: Blackjack By The Book
projects.description:
Blackjack By the Book was created to help teach basic blackjack strategy and let players just play blackjack for fun. Players can create an account to keep track of their performance or sign in as a guest. All standard actions are available for the player, such as Hitting, Staying, Doubling, Splitting, and Surrendering, as appropriate. The game is played with six decks of cards, the dealer must draw to 17, and the dealer hits on soft 17.

The frontend was developed on React 16.7.0 and Redux 4.0.1, and also utilizes React-DOM, React-Router-DOM, and Redux-Thunk. Fetch requests are made to the "Deck of Cards API," which is a third party API that returns the card objects that are used in this game. These fetches occur upon login to set the deck and for player actions involving the cards.

The backend was developed on Ruby 2.5.1 and Rails 5.2.2, and uses Active Model Serializers and a PostgreSQL Database. Once you've created and migrated the database, you will need to seed it with the "Guest" User (already in the seeds.rb rile); this is necessary so that players can sign in as a guest. For basic auth, BCrypt and JWT were used as well.

GitHub Repositories:
https://github.com/mkim4247/Blackjack-By-The-Book-Frontend
https://github.com/mkim4247/Blackjack-By-The-Book-Backend

Project Demo Video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MOIH7OmbQs4

projects.title: On It!
projects.description:
On It was created as a simple project and task management app. Users can create their own private boards to organize personal projects and/or join teams to work on group projects together. Users can create, edit, or delete Boards, which consist of Projects, which further consist of Tasks. They can change the order that Tasks are listed in a Project and/or move the Task to a different Project. They may also leave comments on Projects to ask questions, have discussions, or leave reminders/notes. User can only join a team if they are invited by someone on that team; once a member, they have the option of leaving the team if they want. 

The frontend was developed on React 16.8.1 and Redux 4.0.1, and also utilizes React-DOM, React-Router-DOM, and Redux-Thunk. Semantic-UI-React was used extensively throughout the app as well. React-Beautiful-DnD was incorporated to add drag and drop functionality.

The backend was developed on Ruby 2.5.1 and Rails 5.2.1, and uses Active Model Serializers and a PostgreSQL Database. For basic auth, BCrypt and JWT were used as well.

GitHub Repositories:
https://github.com/mkim4247/On-It-Backend
https://github.com/mkim4247/On-It-Frontend

Project Demo Video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1ENl7yk6aeY
